NationPath Visual Report Share Copy NationPath Brief
 Essential context before you continue reading
 30 sec overview “ The Delhi Government has announced approximately ₹142 crore in LPG-related financial assistance for more than 15 lakh eligible ration-card families. The Diwali instalment is scheduled to be transferred through DBT, providing financial support equivalent to a domestic LPG cylinder rather than distributing physical cylinders.
 Editorial Brief • Quick summary curated for readers NationPath Intelligence
 The Story Behind The News
 Context, analysis and verified insights that explain the story beyond the headline.
 Background
 Context and information behind the story
 The Delhi Cabinet approved the financial assistance scheme in February 2026. Under the announced framework, eligible ration-card-holding families are to receive assistance equivalent to two LPG cylinders every year, with instalments linked to Holi and Diwali.
The assistance is delivered through DBT. The amount differs between PMUY beneficiaries and other eligible households because of the existing central LPG subsidy arrangement.
The government estimated an annual expenditure of around ₹242.77 crore when announcing the scheme. The November announcement represents the Diwali instalment under this framework.
 Key Takeaways
 Important points readers should remember
 More than 15 lakh eligible families are covered by the latest announcement.
 Approximately ₹142 crore is earmarked for the Diwali assistance.
 The benefit is financial assistance through DBT, not physical cylinder distribution.
 Valid and active ration-card eligibility applies.
 The scheme provides for two annual instalments, around Holi and Diwali.
 - Final payment status should be checked through official government communication.
 The Delhi Government is set to provide financial assistance equivalent to the cost of a domestic LPG cylinder to more than 15 lakh eligible ration-card-holding families under its Diwali welfare initiative. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has announced that approximately ₹142 crore will be transferred directly into beneficiaries’ bank accounts through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system.
 The assistance programme is scheduled to be launched from Talkatora Stadium in New Delhi on November 10. Delhi Food and Supplies Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa is also expected to attend the programme.
 Editorial Insight
 Key Highlights
 Important points readers should notice.
 Issue/Event: Diwali LPG financial assistance announced for more than 15 lakh eligible families.
 Location: India.
 Authority/Organisation: Delhi Government, led by Chief Minister Rekha Gupta.
 Action Taken: Approximately ₹142 crore in assistance is scheduled for transfer through Direct Benefit Transfer.
 - Impact: Eligible households are expected to receive financial support towards domestic cooking-gas expenses.
 The initiative is intended to provide relief to households facing cooking-fuel expenses during the festive season. Rather than distributing physical LPG cylinders, the government will transfer the prescribed financial assistance directly to eligible beneficiaries.
 According to the eligibility details announced for the scheme, the benefit is intended for permanent residents of Delhi holding valid and active ration cards registered in the name of the head of the family. The bank and beneficiary details must meet the applicable requirements for DBT payment.
 The assistance amount differs according to the household’s eligibility under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY). Under the scheme’s earlier announced structure, non-Ujjwala households were eligible for assistance equivalent to the full cylinder price, while PMUY beneficiaries were to receive assistance after adjustment of the Centre’s existing subsidy.
 Editorial Analysis
 Why This Matters
 Cooking fuel is a regular household expense, particularly for families managing limited budgets. Direct financial assistance can help eligible households meet part of their LPG costs without requiring them to collect a physical cylinder through a separate distribution process.
The scheme also highlights the role of DBT in delivering welfare benefits directly to bank accounts. Its effectiveness will depend on accurate beneficiary records, successful transfers and timely resolution of payment-related issues.
 The earlier announced reference amounts were ₹853 per cylinder for non-Ujjwala households and ₹553 for PMUY beneficiaries after accounting for the ₹300 central subsidy. These figures may change with applicable LPG prices and subsidy adjustments; beneficiaries should rely on the amount determined for the current payment.
 The Delhi Cabinet approved the broader scheme in February 2026. It provides for financial assistance equivalent to two LPG cylinders annually, with payments scheduled around Holi and Diwali through DBT. The government had estimated an annual expenditure of approximately ₹242.77 crore.
 The latest announcement concerns the Diwali instalment. The actual credit of funds into beneficiaries’ accounts should be confirmed through an official government update after the scheduled programme.
 Future Outlook
 What's Next
 The key next step is confirmation from the Delhi Government that the announced DBT transfer has been completed. Eligible households should monitor their registered bank accounts and official Food and Supplies Department updates for payment information.
The implementation will also need to address any failed transactions or discrepancies in beneficiary and bank details.
